samples.summary: `PATCH /api/v1/.../documents/:did` takes an inline-typed body, so the global ValidationPipe validates nothing — `folderId`/`title` accept arbitrary JSON types (the web twin uses a class-validator DTO)
samples.evidence: `@Body() body: { title?: string; folderId?: string | null }` has metatype `Object`, and `ValidationPipe.toValidate()` skips `Object` metatypes, so the `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted` pipe installed in packages/backend/src/main.ts:65-72 never runs on this handler. An authenticated caller can therefore send `{"folderId": 5}` or `{"folderId": {"contains":"x"}}`; that value goes straight to `FolderService.assertSameWorkspace` → `prisma.folder.findUnique({ where: { id: folderId } })` (folder.service.ts:75), which raises a `PrismaClientValidationError` and surfaces as an unhandled 500 rather than the 400 the web route gives. `data.title = body.title` likewise accepts a Prisma field-update object (`{"set":"x"}`). No injection is reachable (Prisma rejects the wrong scalar type rather than composing it into SQL) and the authorization gate above it still runs, so the impact is error-handling/DoS-noise, not privilege. Contrast the web route, which validates the same fields via `UpdateDocumentDto` (document.controller.ts:314) with `@IsUUID()`, and the sibling folders route, which does use `UpdateFolderDto`.
searchedFor: grep folderId across packages/backend/src to enumerate every writer of Document.folder

samples.summary: `isApiKey → full workspace authority` now also authorizes destructive folder-tree operations, and nothing re-checks that the key's minting user is still an owner/member; removing a member does not revoke their keys
samples.evidence: `isManager()` short-circuits to `true` for any API-key caller (folders.controller.ts:77), and the same short-circuit gates the new document move (documents.controller.ts:128). The only authority proof is `ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard` (write scope) plus `WorkspaceScopeGuard`, which compares `user.workspaceId` to the route param and never consults `WorkspaceMember` for key callers (workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-32). `ApiKeyService.validateKey` checks only hash/revoked/expiry (api-key.service.ts:65-92), and `WorkspaceService.removeMember` deletes the `WorkspaceMember` row without touching `ApiKey` (workspace.service.ts:94-112); the schema has no cascade from membership either (schema.prisma:209-223 — ApiKey cascades on Workspace, not on membership). Vector: an owner mints `wfb_…` with `write`, is later removed from the workspace by another owner, and the still-valid key now passes `isManager()` and can `DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/folders/:folderId` — deleting the folder and, by `Folder.parent onDelete: Cascade` (schema.prisma:137), every descendant folder — for a workspace they no longer belong to. Pre-existing for `documents.remove`, but this change extends the same assumption to the folder tree, so I am flagging it on the new gate; low confidence because keys are plausibly intended as workspace-owned credentials an owner can revoke.
searchedFor: prisma/schema.prisma model ApiKey / model Folder cascade rules

samples.summary: `POST /api/v1/.../documents/:did/copy` is now automation-reachable with no size or quota bound on the blob duplication it triggers
samples.evidence: The handler calls `DocumentCopyService.copy(doc, userId)` with no `dest`, so `fileService.copy(source.fileId)` performs a server-side blob duplication for `pdf`/`image`/`file` documents (document-copy.service.ts:195-199) and a whole-root Yorkie snapshot write for the CRDT types. The service's only resource bounds — `MAX_REHOSTED_IMAGES` / `MAX_REHOSTED_BYTES` (document-copy.service.ts:102-110) — apply solely to the cross-workspace re-hosting path, which a same-workspace copy skips entirely (`workspaceId === source.workspaceId ? undefined : …`, line 233). The only limiter left is the global 120 req/60 s throttler, so a write-scoped API key can amplify workspace storage by ~120×(max upload size) per minute with `wafflebase docs copy` in a loop. The web "Make a copy" has the same exposure, but this change is what makes it reachable by unattended automation. Authenticated-abuse resource exhaustion only — no cross-tenant impact, since the copy is pinned to the source's workspace.
searchedFor: prisma/schema.prisma Document.fileSize comment re: future storage quota

verdict.reason: Every factual link the reviewer asserted checks out, and I could not find the allegedly missing re-check anywhere. folders.controller.ts:77 short-circuits isManager() to true for any API-key caller, and that function is the sole authorization on the destructive DELETE :folderId (folders.controller.ts:146) and the move branch of PATCH (folders.controller.ts:124). Nothing on the key path consults membership: api-key.strategy.ts:22-27 builds req.user from the key row alone; api-key.service.ts:65-93 validates only hash/revokedAt/expiresAt; workspace-scope.guard.ts:26-33 compares user.workspaceId to the route param and returns true for keys (assertMember at line 35 is the JWT branch only); api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:42-48 reads only scopes; combined-auth.guard.ts:16-26 only routes to a strategy. On the revocation side, workspace.service.ts:109-111 deletes just the WorkspaceMember row, packages/backend/src/workspace/** has no reference to apiKey at all, and schema.prisma:209-223 has ApiKey cascading from Workspace with a plain creator relation to User and no relation to WorkspaceMember, so there is no DB-level cascade either. A repo-wide grep for apiKey.update/updateMany/delete/deleteMany yields only ApiKeyService.revoke (api-key.service.ts:58-63, reachable only from the manual owner endpoint api-key.controller.ts:55-63) and a test teardown — no automatic revocation hook, middleware, or job. Vector: an owner mints wfb_... with write scope, is later removed by another owner, and the still-valid key passes isManager() and can DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/folders/:folderId, cascading through descendant folders (schema.prisma Folder.parent onDelete: Cascade) in a workspace they no longer belong to. docs/design/rest-api.md:513-517 documents the "API key acts with workspace authority" short-circuit as intentional, so the short-circuit alone is design intent; what is undocumented and unguarded is the credential lifecycle — an ex-member's unrevoked key keeps full workspace authority, now including folder-tree destruction. That is a real access-control weakness in the security lane, and I found no counterexample to cite against it.
